1.1.0.lead: nexbeat can now request from nexcrate as well, and from this version on this window tells you after each update what changed.

sections.title: Requests to nexcrate
sections.body: Where there was only Lidarr, an administrator can now choose nexcrate. Nothing changes for you: request as usual and follow the state under My requests.
sections.where: Menu at your name › My requests

sections.title: About nexbeat
sections.body: Version, licence and this text now live at the bottom, under “About nexbeat” in the footer. You can open this window again from there.

sections.title: Update hint
sections.body: Once a day nexbeat asks GitHub whether there is a newer version and shows it in the footer and on the page. It can be switched off on the same page.

small: When nexcrate refuses something, its own reason is shown below.
After connecting to nexcrate the library is there at once.

1.1.1.lead: Two repairs: requests to a slow nexcrate, and artists who share a name.

sections.title: Requests to a slow nexcrate
sections.body: When nexcrate took longer than a minute to answer, nexbeat showed error 504 although the request had arrived, and sent it a second time in the background. nexbeat now hands a request over in the background and never sends the same one twice at once. Until nexcrate has taken it, the request says "Handing over".
sections.where: Menu at your name › My requests

sections.title: Artists who share a name
sections.body: Artists of the same name all got the photo and the top tracks of the best known one. Both now come by the artist's MusicBrainz entry, and search tells namesakes apart by country and description.

1.2.0.lead: nexbeat now has API tokens. With one, dashboards like nexdeck show your requests, and administrators approve requests right from the dashboard.

sections.title: API tokens
sections.body: In your profile you create tokens for scripts and dashboards. A token has exactly your rights; ticked “Read only” it can neither request nor change anything. It is shown once, sent as the header Authorization: Bearer … and can be revoked at any time.
sections.where: Menu at your name › Profile › API tokens

sections.title: nexbeat in nexdeck
sections.body: With a token nexdeck shows waiting, running and failed requests, the library and, for administrators, the requests to approve with buttons to approve and turn down. The buttons need the token of an administrator that may write.
sections.where: Menu at your name › Profile › API tokens

sections.title: Who has which tokens
sections.body: Under Users you see which accounts created tokens and when they were last used. Only its owner can revoke a token; deactivating an account locks its tokens too.

small: Changing your password leaves tokens working. Revoke the ones you no longer need in your profile.
The interface for your own scripts is under /api/v1 and described at /api/docs.

1.3.0.lead: You can now sign in through authentik, Microsoft Entra ID, Keycloak, Authelia, Pocket ID and any other OpenID Connect provider. nexbeat sets up authentik by itself in one click.

sections.title: Sign in with your provider
sections.body: The sign-in page has a button for every provider that is set up. If you already have an account, link it once in your profile; after that you can sign in without a password. Whoever joins through a provider can set a password of their own there later.
sections.where: Menu at your name › Profile › Sign-in providers

sections.title: authentik in one step
sections.body: With the address of authentik and an API token, nexbeat creates its provider and application there and adds itself as a sign-in provider. The token is used for this only and is not stored. If you would rather not hand over a token, download a blueprint instead.

sections.title: Add a provider yourself
sections.body: Any OpenID Connect provider can be added by hand, Microsoft Entra ID with one or many tenants included. For each provider you decide whether new accounts are created on first sign-in, and with which role.

small: Accounts are matched only by the provider's ID for a person, never by email address. An existing account gets to a provider only through the link in the profile.
A provider through which accounts without a password were created can only be deleted after a confirmation.
